title: The Last Victory of Rome
hook: Part 6. Can Rome’s greatest enemy still save Carthage at home?
full_narration: Part 6. Can Rome’s greatest enemy still save Carthage at home? In 202 BCE, Hannibal faces Scipio on the plain of Zama. [[pause:0.4]] His war elephants surge forward, but Roman lanes open like traps. By sunset, Scipio defeats Hannibal, and Carthage’s last gamble collapses. [[voice:tense]] In 201 BCE, Carthage accepts peace under Rome’s hard shadow. Its fleet is surrendered, its wars forbidden, its tribute chained to decades. [[pause:0.6]] In Rome, Scipio receives honors and a new name: Africanus. The victor becomes legend, while Hannibal returns as something stranger. In 196 BCE, Hannibal becomes suffete, a statesman in a wounded city. [[voice:low]] He reforms Carthage’s finances, making payments possible and corruption dangerous. From 195 BCE, Roman pressure drives Hannibal from Carthage into exile. In 183 BCE, he dies in Bithynia, but Carthage keeps recovering. [[pause:0.8]] Follow for part 7.

youtube_description: Part 6 of The Fall of Carthage follows Hannibal’s final turn from battlefield legend to political survivor. In 202 BCE, he faces Scipio at Zama, where Rome wins the battle that decides the Second Punic War. Carthage survives, but only under harsh peace terms. Scipio becomes Africanus, while Hannibal becomes suffete and tries to repair his wounded city through financial reform. But Rome still fears him. Pressure forces him into exile, and he later dies far from Carthage in Bithynia. Yet the city he left behind begins to recover, and that recovery will awaken Rome’s old fear again.
